I have farmed these 14 mu in Quzhou for 40 years. I finished middle school, so I can read fertilizer bags and do sums, but I learn from doing and from watching my neighbors. My family has six people, and my son and daughter-in-law work in a factory in Handan, so they send money home. That helps, but I still watch every yuan. I would rather spend a little more on fertilizer than risk a bad harvest — a failed crop is a disaster, but extra fertilizer is just a cost I can absorb.

This year I will keep the same layout as last year: 8 mu for wheat-maize rotation, 4 mu for garlic, and 2 mu for cotton. I do not change what works. For the 8 mu of winter wheat, I will plant Jimai 22, an improved variety I have used for five years. I rotary till before seeding in early October and put 30 jin of seed per mu. For fertilizer, I spread one 50-kg bag of compound fertilizer per mu as base, then top-dress with urea at green-up and jointing. In total that comes to about 28 kg of nitrogen, 12 kg of phosphorus, and 10 kg of potassium per mu. I irrigate three times from my well: before winter freeze, at jointing in March, and at grain filling in May. I spray twice — once with herbicide after seeding, and once with insecticide if I see aphids. Last year I got 550 kg per mu, and I expect the same this year.

After harvesting wheat in early June, I immediately plant summer maize on the same 8 mu. I use hybrid seed, about 5 jin per mu. I do not plough — I plant directly into the wheat stubble with a no-till planter. I put compound fertilizer in the row at planting and side-dress urea when the plants are knee-high. That is 25 kg nitrogen, 10 kg phosphorus, and 8 kg potassium per mu. I irrigate three times in July and August when it gets dry, and I spray three times: herbicide at seeding, then insecticide for corn borer and armyworm. I expect 650 kg per mu if the rain cooperates.

My 2 mu of cotton is hard work. I deep plough in April because cotton roots need loose soil. I plant an improved Bt variety, about 2 jin of seed per mu. I use one 50-kg bag of compound fertilizer per mu and top-dress twice with urea, totaling 20 kg nitrogen, 10 kg phosphorus, and 10 kg potassium per mu. Cotton needs water during flowering, so I irrigate four times, especially in July and August. I spray four times for bollworm, aphids, and mites. I expect 120 kg of seed cotton per mu.

The 4 mu of garlic is where I make my best money. Quzhou garlic sells well. I plant my own traditional cloves, about 400 jin per mu, in mid-October. I rotary till and make flat beds. Garlic needs a lot of food: I put two 50-kg bags of compound fertilizer per mu as base and top-dress with urea twice in spring. That is 28 kg nitrogen, 15 kg phosphorus, and 15 kg potassium per mu. I irrigate five times: right after planting, before winter, at green-up in March, when the scape elongates in April, and during bulb swelling in May. I spray three times for rust and thrips. Last year I harvested 3,000 jin per mu, so I expect 1,500 kg per mu this year.

I figure my total fertilizer cost will be around 4,500 yuan. That is a lot, but my son's remittance covers it. I hire three day-laborers for garlic harvest in May and two for cotton picking in September — my wife and I cannot do it all alone. I watch what Old Wang does across the road. He puts similar amounts on his wheat and maize, and his yields are always good, so I copy him. At my age, I do not try new tricks. If last year was fine, this year will be the same.
